correctness.rationale: For each orientation the zero output is the kernel of an equality graph, of dimension its component count; nonuniform ring orientations have precisely k adjacent (+,-) two-cycles, while the two uniform orientations require one extra count. The two-state transfer matrix has trace one and determinant -lambda(1-lambda), giving the closed formula. A Lucas-polynomial even-part identity yields positive coefficients, strict optimization, and the dominant-root asymptotic. Exact-rational direct state/rule enumeration, GF(2) nullity checks, and a separate recurrence agree for 295 parameter/size combinations. No finite test is taken as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The one-step extinction chance of the all-zero absorbing state is a directly motivated finite-size observable for the paper's central absorbing-state model. Exact all-n and all-lambda classification collapses an exponential joint sum to a 2x2 transfer matrix and reveals that balanced sitewise stochasticity has a strict and exponentially amplifying advantage over either deterministic rule. This offers a concrete benchmark for absorption simulations and clarifies a finite-size phenomenon not accessible from one-point density approximations. No claim of global phase-transition behavior or eventual absorption time is needed.
